text: These are the nations the LORD left in place to test Israel through them—all those Israelites who had not known any of the wars of Canaan.

versions.text: These are the nations the LORD left in place to test Israel by them—all those Israelites who had not known any of the wars for Canaan.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew construct מִלְחֲמוֹת כְּנָעַן means "the wars of Canaan" (i.e., the wars fought in Canaan). "Wars for Canaan" introduces a purpose idea not present in the Hebrew and reads awkwardly aloud.

versions.text: These are the nations the LORD left in place to test Israel by them—all those Israelites who had not known any of the wars of Canaan.
versions.explanation: The instrumental בָּם is more naturally rendered "through them" in English; "by them" can momentarily read as an agent-of-passive or a locative phrase when heard aloud, whereas "through them" keeps the instrumental sense clear in oral reading.

text: He did this only so that the generations of Israel might learn warfare—those, at least, who had known nothing of it before.
The nations were these: the five rulers of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
They were left to test Israel, to find out whether they would obey the commandments the LORD had given their fathers through Moses.
So the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
They took their daughters as wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
So the land had rest for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
Eglon gathered to himself the Ammonites and the Amalekites, and he went and struck Israel down, and they took possession of the City of Palms.
So the Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.

Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword about a cubit long, and he strapped it under his clothing on his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the men who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the carved stones near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" and all who were standing by him withdrew from his presence.

versions.text: But he himself turned back at the carved stones near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" and all his attendants left the room.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says "all who stood by him went out from him"; "left the room" adds a detail (a room) not in the text and loses the idiom of attendants withdrawing from the king's presence.

text: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper chamber, and Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." And the king rose from his seat.

versions.text: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper chamber, and Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." As the king rose from his seat,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause is a complete statement ("and he arose from the seat"). Ending the verse with a dangling subordinate clause and a comma is awkward for oral reading, since the next verse begins a new sentence.

text: Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon's belly.
Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over it, for he did not pull the sword out of his belly; and the filth came out.
Then Ehud went out to the porch, closing the doors of the upper chamber behind him and locking them.
After he had gone, the king's servants came and saw that the doors of the upper chamber were locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool inner room."
They waited until they were embarrassed, and still he did not open the doors of the upper chamber. So they took the key and opened them—and there lay their lord, fallen dead on the floor.
Ehud had escaped while they delayed. He passed the carved stones and got away to Seirah.
When he arrived, he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hills, with him at their head.

He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand." So they followed him down and seized the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, letting no one cross over.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men; not one escaped.
That day Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too delivered Israel.
